args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of v2.3.1, checkout-api failed health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), with an error rate of 18%. v2.3.1 is unhealthy in production, and its release candidate v2.3.1-rc was also unhealthy in staging. Rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback the service is healthy on v2.3.0 in all regions and the error rate is 0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure before redeploying it, and review why it was released when the staging RC was unhealthy.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's now passing health checks. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** Every region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was on v2.3.1, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the next steps: find out why v2.3.1 failed before redeploying it. Also find out why it was released when its test build (v2.3.1-rc) was already failing in staging.
- **Retry:** The first attempt to open the incident timed out. I checked the incident list, saw nothing had been created, and tried again using the same request ID. That way it couldn't create a duplicate incident or page on-call twice.

No approval was needed: the policy only requires one for deploying a version that has never been healthy in production, and v2.3.0 has been.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.

content.text:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions, and it's now passing health checks. I also opened SEV2 incident INC-0001, which paged on-call.

- **Rollback:** Every region (us-east, us-west, eu-west) was on v2.3.1, failing health checks with an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0 and the error rate is 0.2%.
- **Incident:** It describes the failure, the rollback and the next steps: find out why v2.3.1 failed before redeploying it. Also find out why it was released when its test build (v2.3.1-rc) was already failing in staging.
- **Retry:** The first attempt to open the incident timed out. I checked the incident list, saw nothing had been created, and tried again using the same request ID. That way it couldn't create a duplicate incident or page on-call twice.

No approval was needed: the policy only requires one for deploying a version that has never been healthy in production, and v2.3.0 has been.
